name: Astroblastoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System

criteria.description: Presence of characteristic astroblastic pseudorosettes on histological examination
MRI showing well-circumscribed, often cystic supratentorial mass with heterogeneous enhancement
Positive GFAP (glial fibrillary acidic protein) staining with variable EMA expression
Identification of MN1 gene rearrangement in tumor cells

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of astroblastic pseudorosettes combined with characteristic imaging and immunohistochemical findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular testing for MN1 rearrangement supports diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal neurological deficits related to tumor location
Seizures originating from tumor-affected cortical areas

common.symptomName: Headache due to increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: head pain from increased intracranial pressure

common.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting secondary to raised intracranial pressure
searchTerms: vomiting caused by increased intracranial pressure

common.symptomName: Visual disturbances from optic pathway involvement
searchTerms: seeing disturbances related to optic pathway
problems with language or slurred speech
speech impairment or trouble finding words
weakness on one side of the body

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction due to hypothalamic involvement
searchTerms: hormone problems from brain area damage
endocrine issues due to hypothalamus involvement
hormonal imbalance caused by brain tumor
fluid buildup in brain from tumor blockage
brain swelling due to blocked fluid flow
water on the brain caused by tumor
cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems

laboratory: CSF analysis typically non-specific but may show elevated protein
imaging: MRI: well-demarcated supratentorial mass with cystic and solid components
Contrast enhancement heterogeneous with possible peritumoral edema
genetic: MN1 gene rearrangement detected by FISH or molecular methods
Absence of IDH1/2 mutations differentiates from diffuse gliomas
other: Histopathology: astroblastic pseudorosettes with perivascular hyalinization
Immunohistochemistry: GFAP positive, variable EMA positivity

distinguishingFeatures: Ependymomas show true ependymal rosettes rather than astroblastic pseudorosettes
More common in posterior fossa and spinal cord
Different molecular profile without MN1 rearrangement
Pilocytic astrocytomas have biphasic pattern with Rosenthal fibers
Typically occur in children and young adults with cystic lesions and mural nodules
Lack astroblastic pseudorosettes and MN1 rearrangement

redFlags: New onset seizures in young adults
Signs of increased intracranial pressure such as persistent vomiting and papilledema
references: Louis DN, Perry A, Wesseling P, et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition. IARC; 2021.
Parker NR, Khong P, Parkinson JF, et al. Molecular heterogeneity in astroblastoma: MN1 rearrangement defines a distinct clinicopathologic entity. Acta Neuropathol. 2016.
